title: Capacity surge spline forecast & variant matrix (NA/EU/APAC)
content:
Purpose:
A compact, decision-ready capacity forecast that models three rollout waves across NA / EU / APAC for TPU/GPU mixes and utilization sensitivity. This is a working sheet (variant matrix) to support commit conversations with cloud vendors and to feed Dedicated onboarding windows. Not final — assumptions listed below.

Executive summary:
- Target window: Nov 2025 -> Jul 2027 (24 months view with emphasis on H1–H2 2026).
- Core ask: 11k effective vGPU slots by end-2026 in NA, 6k in EU, 4k in APAC (effective slots = normalized by model-mix).
- Preferred execution: rolling waves (wave A: feature-latency tier, wave B: cost-optimized, wave C: buffer/burst).

Key assumptions (short):
- Average model mix weight: 60% decoder-only large, 30% instruction-tuned medium, 10% embeddings-only.
- Average seq len (prod): 96 tokens; peak seq len for 99p planning: 512 tokens.
- Target long-run utilization: 55% steady-state; surge planning to 80% for max 7-day windows.
- Effective slot conversion: A100-80GB = 1.0, A100-40GB = 0.6, H100 = 1.2, T4-like = 0.12 (normalized).

Quarterly projection table (normalized slots) - baseline scenario:
| Quarter | NA target | EU target | APAC target | Notes |
| Q4 2025 | 1,200 | 500 | 250 | initial warm pools, reserved burst |
| Q1 2026 | 3,000 | 1,200 | 600 | wave A expansion (latency tier) |
| Q2 2026 | 6,500 | 2,800 | 1,300 | wave B (cost-optimized on new SKUs) |
| Q3 2026 | 9,000 | 4,200 | 2,400 | wave C buffer + canary capacity |
| Q4 2026 | 11,000 | 6,000 | 4,000 | target committed baseline |

Rollout windows and gating triggers:
- Wave A (Nov 2025–Mar 2026): must achieve per-request p50 latency <= 120ms for 2k qps baseline on NA; gating ticket: JIRA-OPS-2982.
- Wave B (Apr 2026–Jun 2026): cost-optimized fleet onboarding, enable auto-quantization pipelines; gating: 10% unit-cost improvement on sampled workloads.
- Wave C (Jul 2026–Dec 2026): buffer lanes, cross-region failover readiness, dedicated reserved commitments.

Surge / contingency lanes:
- Hot spare policy: maintain 6–8% of effective slots as immediate warm spare per region during Q2–Q4 2026.
- Fallback stack: route non-critical traffic to quantized model variants or lower tier (T4) with price delta bounds.
- Emergency throttle triggers: sustained error rate > 1.5% OR latency p95 > 3x SLO for 15m -> invoke cross-region spill to EU (for NA incidents) with graceful degradation policy.

Utilization sensitivity variants (short):
- Conservative: plan to 45% steady utilization -> requires +20% slots over baseline.
- Baseline: 55% utilization -> baseline numbers above.
- Aggressive: 65% utilization with improved batching & caching -> reduces slot needs by ~12%.

Open risks and mitigation:
- GPU procurement lead times unpredictable (mitigation: stagger vendor mix, maintain 10% buffer in procurement pipeline).
- Software perf regressions during model rollouts (mitigation: pre-rollout perf benching, canary scheduling).
- Inter-region network egress cost spikes (mitigation: prefer region-local caches and KV cache population priming).

Immediate action items (owner -> due):
- Confirm vendor lead ETA for H100 lot (Marcus Li -> 2025-10-23).
- Run cost-sensitivity sim for quantized vs fp16 mixes (Ava Chen -> 2025-10-16).
- Add canary routing rule to staging for Wave B (Diego Martinez -> 2025-11-02).

Notes to reviewers:
- This sheet is intentionally conservative in slot-normalization; please call out if you have updated SKU equivalence.
- I shoved quick numbers into a table for planning — we should convert to a canonical sheet with per-SKU rows before vendor commit.

Appendix (short):
- Reference conversion matrix used for baseline sizing: (H100=1.2, A100-80=1.0, A100-40=0.6, T4=0.12).
- Related tickets/PRs listed in linked_artifacts.

Unresolved questions:
1) Do we want to prioritize regional reserved contracts (long-term discounts) vs vendor spot/commit mix for Wave B?
2) Should we pre-seed model-specific KV caches in APAC to reduce warmup spikes on go-live?

End of sheet.
